title: Sandbox Setup and Credentials
subtitle: From an empty settings page to a token LHDN accepts, without putting a production invoice at risk
outcomes: Register for the MyInvois sandbox and obtain client credentials
Distinguish the sandbox and production hosts, and know why mixing them fails
Fill the settings form correctly, including timeouts, retries and default tax type
Validate a TIN against LHDN and use the result to clean up master data
Keep secrets out of tickets, screenshots and source control

slides.title: Two environments, two sets of hosts
bullets: Sandbox uses preprod-api and preprod-identity hosts; production uses api and identity
Credentials are issued per environment and are not interchangeable
Sandbox documents are disposable: they exist to rehearse, so never reconcile from them
The app's Environment setting selects the host pair, so a wrong value looks like an authentication failure
Treat the switch to Production as a change request, not a dropdown tweak
slides.notes: The most common first-day mistake is a production client id with the environment left on Sandbox, or the reverse. The symptom is a token error that reads like a credentials problem, which sends people to reset secrets they did not need to touch. Show the two host pairs explicitly so the learner can reason about which pair their instance is talking to.

slides.title: Getting client credentials from the portal
bullets: Register the taxpayer in the MyInvois portal, then open the Taxpayer System area
Create an integration to receive a client id and client secret for that taxpayer
The client id identifies the system; the secret authenticates it and must be rotated when staff change
Intermediaries also need an On Behalf Of TIN, which becomes onbehalfof in the token request
Record who created the integration and where the secret is stored before you close the browser tab
slides.notes: Portal navigation changes, so teach the shape rather than the pixel positions: taxpayer, then integration, then credentials. The On Behalf Of field only applies to intermediaries acting for another taxpayer; if you are not one, leaving it blank is correct. Insist on a named owner for the integration, because it is the thing you cannot recover from a backup.

slides.title: Filling the settings form, field by field
bullets: Enable Malaysia e-Invoicing is off by default, so the hooks do nothing until you switch it on
Submit Automatically on Sales Invoice Submit decides whether submission is queued or manual
Use Short Queue sends jobs to the short queue for faster turnaround during testing
Request Timeout defaults to 30 seconds and Max Retries to 3; raise them only with evidence
Default Classification and Default Tax Type are fallbacks, not substitutes for correct master data

rows: Stay here until the readiness gate passes
Turn off for the first production week
Required for B2C and consolidated invoices
Raise only for slow links, never to mask failures
Use 01 or 02 if you are SST registered

slides.notes: Defaults encode opinions, so explain them. Automatic submission is right for a steady state and wrong for a first production week, when a human should read each result. A default tax type of 06 is correct for a business that is not SST registered and dangerously wrong for one that is, because the tax amount then quietly disappears from the payload.

slides.title: How the token flow behaves under pressure
bullets: The client requests a token with client_credentials and the InvoicingAPI scope
Tokens are cached per identity host, client id and on-behalf-of combination, with a 60-second safety margin
A 401 triggers exactly one refresh and retry, which absorbs ordinary expiry without alarming users
Repeated 401s mean credentials, environment or taxpayer status, not a network problem
Every authentication failure is written to the submission log, so support has evidence
slides.notes: The one-refresh rule exists to avoid infinite loops. If a token is rejected twice, something structural is wrong: the secret was rotated, the taxpayer was suspended, or the environment is wrong. Teach the learner to read the error body rather than retry blindly. Caching matters in production because token requests are the most common source of rate limiting.

slides.title: Validate TINs before you invoice, not after
bullets: The client exposes LHDN's taxpayer validate endpoint for a TIN plus identity type and value
A 200 means the identity exists and matches; a 404 means it does not
Use validation as a cleanup project for your top hundred customers, not as a per-invoice gate
Incorrect TINs are a master data defect, and the fix belongs in the customer record
Re-validate quarterly, because registrations are cancelled and businesses are struck off
slides.notes: Explain the difference between a format check and a registry check. The app validates TIN format locally and can ask LHDN whether the identity exists. The second is authoritative but rate limited, so the sensible pattern is bulk validation, then periodic re-validation. If a customer's TIN fails, do not invent one: issue to General Public or ask the customer.

slides.title: Timezones, currencies and the fields that surprise people
bullets: Issue time is converted from the site timezone to UTC and written with a trailing Z
Issue date comes from the posting date, so back-dated invoices are not necessarily rejected but are visible
Documents must be in ringgit, so foreign currency invoices are refused rather than converted
The buyer address needs a Malaysian state code, which the app derives from the state name
Quantities lose trailing zeros, so two units are sent as 2 rather than 2.0000
slides.notes: UTC conversion is the quiet source of off-by-one-day confusion: a 7am invoice in Kuala Lumpur is the previous day in UTC. LHDN compares dates in its own way, so keep posting dates honest. The currency rule is a policy trap: a company that invoices in USD needs a converted MYR invoice for LHDN, and that has accounting consequences which should be decided before go-live.

slides.title: Secrets, roles and who may press submit
bullets: The secret lives in a password field and is masked in the interface, but it can still be copied by an administrator
Only System Manager should be able to edit settings; accounts staff need read access at most
Never paste a secret into a ticket, a chat or a screenshot; rotate it if you do
Define who may submit and who may cancel, and make the second list much shorter
Keep submission logs readable to accounts and auditors but not editable by them
slides.notes: Frappe's password fields are encrypted at rest but retrievable by privileged users, so role design carries the real weight. The two-person rule for cancellation is a governance control, not a technical one, and it belongs in the same policy document as the reason templates from chapter one. Rotating a secret is a five-minute job; a leaked secret is a compliance incident.

slides.title: The first end-to-end proof on sandbox
bullets: Run settings_status and fix every field it reports as missing
Validate your own TIN and one customer TIN, and record the responses
Preview a simple invoice and read the generated UBL JSON plus its hash
Submit it, then watch the log move from Queued to Submitted and eventually Valid
Cancel it with a reason and confirm LHDN returns a cancelled state with the reason recorded

callout.title: One invoice, all six states
callout.text: A single sandbox invoice can show you Queued, Submitted, Valid, Cancelled and, if you corrupt the data, Invalid. That is the cheapest education you will get.

slides.notes: This is the rehearsal that makes production boring. Ask the learner to screenshot each state, because screenshots become the training material for the accounts team. If validation never completes, check the scheduler before you suspect the app: a site with no scheduler looks exactly like a broken polling loop.

lab.title: Wire up sandbox and prove the whole loop
steps: Create or log in to a MyInvois sandbox taxpayer and generate integration credentials
Enter client id, secret and Environment Sandbox in Malaysia E-Invoice Settings and save
Run settings_status and confirm it no longer reports missing credentials
Validate your own company TIN through the app's validate endpoint and read the response
Create a customer with a valid sandbox TIN, a primary address and a postcode
Preview a one-line invoice, copy the hash, then submit it and wait for the log to reach Valid
Record the UUID on the invoice, then cancel the e-Invoice with a reason under 300 characters
Refresh the status and confirm the log and the invoice both show the cancelled state
lab.done: The log holds a Valid document with a UUID and a hash, your cancellation appears with its reason, and you can name the host pair your site was talking to at each step.

quiz.question: You pasted production credentials but the environment still says Sandbox. What happens?
options: It works, because credentials determine the host
The token request goes to the sandbox identity host and fails
The app silently switches to production
LHDN returns a 404 on the invoice
quiz.why: The environment setting picks the host pair. Sandbox credentials are unknown to the sandbox host, and the failure looks like an authentication error.

quiz.question: What does a 401 from MyInvois usually mean in this app?
options: The invoice totals do not reconcile
Credentials, environment or taxpayer status need attention after the automatic refresh
The MSIC code is invalid
Nothing: 401 is retried forever
quiz.why: One refresh is attempted transparently. A second 401 means the secret, the environment or the taxpayer account is wrong, and retrying will not help.

quiz.question: Why validate TINs in bulk rather than on every invoice?
options: LHDN charges per validation
It adds a rate-limited call to every invoice and turns a data problem into an availability problem
Validation is only valid for 24 hours
Bulk validation is more accurate
quiz.why: A missing invoice cannot wait on a registry call. Clean masters in bulk, then re-validate periodically so stale TINs are caught.

quiz.question: A foreign currency Sales Invoice reaches the app. What should you expect?
options: It is converted automatically at the company exchange rate
It is rejected locally because only MYR is supported
It is submitted with DocumentCurrencyCode set to the invoice currency
It is queued until the currency changes
quiz.why: MyInvois accepts ringgit only, so the app validates the currency and blocks submission rather than inventing a conversion.

quiz.question: Status is stuck on Submitted and never becomes Valid. What should you check first?
options: The client secret
Whether the site scheduler is running, because polling is a scheduled job
The customer's postcode
The invoice naming series
quiz.why: Validation is asynchronous and polling runs on the scheduler. Without it, documents sit at Submitted indefinitely even though LHDN has already validated them.

narration: Chapter three is about getting connected without breaking anything. MyInvois has two environments with separate hosts and separate credentials: sandbox on preprod, production on api. The app's environment setting chooses the host pair, which is why a production client id left on sandbox looks like a credentials failure. Get credentials from the taxpayer system in the portal, create an integration, and write down who owns it, because the secret is the one thing you cannot recover from a backup. In settings, defaults matter more than they look. Automatic submission is right for steady state and wrong for your first production week. A default tax type of zero six is correct if you are not SST registered, and quietly wrong if you are. The client requests a token with client credentials and caches it with a sixty second safety margin, refreshing once on a four zero one. If a four zero one repeats, stop retrying: the secret, the environment or the taxpayer account is wrong. Validate TINs in bulk, not on every invoice, because a missing invoice should never wait on a registry call. Remember that issue time is converted to UTC, that documents must be in ringgit, and that a buyer address needs a Malaysian state code. Then prove the loop: run the health check, validate a TIN, preview, submit, wait for valid, and cancel with a reason. In the lab you do exactly that, and you keep the screenshots as training material.
